sections.title: Against the outcome
sections.lead: This is the only case in the project with a documented outcome, and the only place any of the method's claims can be scored at all.
sections.html:
The three tests, and all three now score

1
Centre inside ×1.3 pass
1423 against 1663 person-days — ×1.17 low. Both classification repeats are inside on their own: 1400 and 1446.
2
The declared corridor contains the outcome pass, first time
1121–1725 contains 1663, which sits at about P85. This test had never been scoreable, because the chain declared no corridor. Read the provenance clause below before reading this as a result.
3
Nothing fitted on the case pass
No rate, no factor and no classification was chosen while looking at the outcome. The one level factor ever fitted here was withdrawn when the unit error under it was found.

What the corridor's pass does and does not mean

The corridor rests on one declared number — the correlation between work items, ρ = 0.5. That number was not fitted on this case: it was declared while working the other case, on the general reasoning that the truth is neither 0 nor 1 and far from both. But it was declared with this outcome already on the record and known. So it is not fitted, and it is not blind. A corridor whose width parameter is chosen after the answer is visible is weaker evidence than one chosen before, and this report says so rather than counting the pass at full weight.

And the case has stopped being able to score anything further

Three conditions of the case arrived from the outcome's owner after the estimate existed: staffed-versus-delivered time, the presence fraction, and the headcount on the concept stage. Each was legitimate — each was a real input nobody had asked for. The last is one sixth of the answer by arithmetic: ten people for two of twelve months. A gate cleared by being handed a sixth of the answer is not a gate.

The rule the episode produced, and it costs nothing to apply from now on: a case profile is pinned with the requirements, before any estimate — team grade and domain experience, declared overheads and what is inside them, the presence fraction, the process, and the staffing of every stage the method prices separately. All of it was obtainable on day one, from the same person. A case whose conditions arrive after its number can be learned from; it cannot score.

One parameter still undeclared, and it is on the outcome's side

The outcome is recorded as 120 staffed person-months — ten people on the staff for about a year, from a participant's memory, stated at ±20%. Turning that into working time needs the presence fraction: how much of a nominal staffed year is actually present. At 0.88 the outcome is 1663 person-days and the miss is ×1.17; across the plausible 0.83–0.91 it runs ×1.10 to ×1.21. The verdict does not turn on it, but the figure is not declared and should be.

sections.title: The outside view
sections.lead: The first reference-class reading on this case in this generation. It never saw the product model, the work items, the rate table or any number from the chain — and it produced its estimate in the unit the outcome is natively recorded in, which makes one comparison here exact and another impossible.
sections.html:
What it says

P10P50P80P90P95P99
person-months, funded seats70140225290380620
ratio to its own median0.501.001.612.072.714.43

The one comparison on this page that needs no conversion

Its unit is the funded-seat person-month — seats multiplied by elapsed time, all roles, leave inside, no focus factor applied. The outcome is recorded in exactly that unit: ten staffed heads for about a year. Both sides are seats × time, so the comparison is direct and no convention enters it:

class 140 against an outcome of 120 — ×1.17 high. The outcome sits at about P39 of the class distribution.

Every other comparison this project has made needed a conversion on one side or the other. This one does not, and it is the first.

How it is placed on the chart

The chart is in net hours of work on the task and this reading is in funded seats. The conversion between them is not a guess — it is a ladder, and only its last rung is contested:

one funded seat, one yeardays leftdetermined by
calendar365arithmetic
less weekends261arithmetic
less public holidays, ~10251a fact of the case's country
less annual leave, ~10–15238the organisation's policy
less sickness, ~5233the organisation's average

That gives a presence fraction of 0.893. The sensor's own figure is 19.3 ÷ 21.7 = 0.889; this report declares 0.88. Three independent sources, one number — this rung is closed.

The last rung is how many of a present day's eight nominal hours are work on the task. What comes out inside the day: standups, planning and review meetings, code review given and received, design discussion, context switching, waiting on other people, reading, rework, ordinary friction. This project declares 6. The sensor declares 4.0–5.6. That is the whole of the disagreement, and it is worth ×1.25 on where the blue curve sits — nothing else in the ladder is open.

1 funded-seat person-month = 21 weekdays × 0.88 presence × 6 net task hours ÷ 8 = 13.86 person-days.

That is the same conversion the outcome is placed by, which is why the class and the outcome keep their exact ratio of ×1.17 whatever convention is chosen — both are funded seats, and the factor cancels. It does not cancel against the bottom-up, which is native to task hours: at the sensor's own 4.8 hours the blue curve would sit at 1552 rather than 1940, left of the outcome instead of right of it.

What the blue curve actually is

It is the sensor's own declared body — a lognormal with σ = 0.55 — and not an interpolation between its quantiles. That distinction matters: interpolating between stated points produces a flat block between P10 and P50 and destroys the mode, so the curve comes out looking like a descending ramp rather than a distribution. The declared lognormal reproduces the sensor's own P10, P80 and P90 to within 1–2%, and puts the mode at about 1434 — left of the median, as a right-skewed body has it.

Two honest edges. Nothing below P10 was stated, and the lognormal supplies that region from its own shape rather than from anything the sensor said. And the stated P95 sits about 9% above the lognormal, because the sensor lifted its tail deliberately, saying the extreme tail of IT outcomes is heavier than lognormal and giving its reason; the drawn curve does not carry that lift.

The class it constructed

Not looked up — built for this project at run time, with membership stated as categories of work that must be present and categories that must be absent:

Replacement of an already-operating revenue-bearing back-end system, built in-house by a product company's own blended team, where the central engineering difficulty is sustained-throughput distributed processing with per-item delivery guarantees, in a pre-cloud era with hand-built infrastructure, by a team new to the business domain, with a definition of done that requires parallel operation against the predecessor and its decommissioning.

55% confidence in that class, with 20 points of the remainder moving the answer up and 25 points moving it down. It named misclassification as the largest single source of error in its own forecast — larger than the sampling error inside the class.

Its shape is triple-sourced; its level is single-sourced — and it says so

The ratios P10/P50 = 0.50 and P90/P50 = 2.07 fall out of three sources of different provenance that agree: the published cone of uncertainty, a systematic review of estimation studies, and a large-sample study of outcomes. Every person-month of the level, by contrast, descends from one anchor — team size multiplied by calendar duration.

If this forecast is wrong, the most probable failure is that A1 or A2 is wrong for this project, and not that the ratios are wrong. Anyone reconciling this sensor against another should attack the level first and leave the ratios alone.

The contamination residue it declared against itself

The input carried the calendar window — "roughly 2007–2009" — and its principal anchor is built as team × duration, so a duration hint is a live path into its level. It raised this unprompted, bounded the possible nudge at ±15% on the median, said it could not bound it tighter, and recommended stripping the window from any future run. The duration band it used, 12–24 months, is not pulled toward the hint; that is a fact about its declared anchor, not a measure of how much the hint mattered.

And a tail with its own truncation caveat

It refused to continue a lognormal past P90, on the ground that the extreme tail of IT outcomes is heavier than lognormal, and lifted P95 and P99 by hand. Then it cut against itself: a product company of this size cannot fund a 620-person-month rework of a system it already owns, so the class's own economics delete the project rather than fund it.

My P95 and P99 are probably too high as predictors of recorded effort, and about right as predictors of required effort. These two diverge only above P90; below it they coincide.

sections.title: How to read the chart
sections.lead: One distribution and one line. The line is what happened; the distribution is what the method said before anyone looked.
sections.html:
Where the distribution comes from

Every rate cell carries an optimistic, a most-likely and a pessimistic value. The chain collapsed each to its expected value before summing, so the range existed at the leaf and was destroyed at the total. Restoring it needs one declared number: how strongly the 543 priced items are correlated. Both ends are wrong — independent gives a P10–P90 of ×1.04, which would claim the total is known to ±1%; perfectly correlated gives ×1.86. ρ = 0.5 is declared, and across ρ from 0.25 to 0.75 the band edges move about ±20%.

ΣO…ΣP — every optimistic and every pessimistic end summed — spans ×4.14 here. That is six sigma, the absolute extremes, not a percentile band; a P10–P90 is 2.56 sigma.

Why there is no outside view on this chart

The reference-class sensor has not run on this case in this generation. It produced two readings for it in 2026 — and both are in units that were never declared, which is why the four cross-generation readings that rested on them are currently suspended rather than quoted. Drawing them here would put quantities of unknown dimension on a scale with a known one.

The consequence is worth stating plainly: this case has no second opinion. The one number on this chart comes from one method, and what checks it is not another instrument but the outcome.

The unit

Person-days of 8 net hours of work on the task, 40 to the week. Leave, public holidays and sickness are not in these numbers, and neither is any notion of calendar or headcount. If you need days of presence, divide by the effective task hours your working day delivers — commonly 5 to 6, never 8 — and add your own allowance for leave.

That unit cost this project three days and three separate errors, all the same shape: the outcome recorded as headcount × calendar and read as delivered work; a conversion applied to one side of the comparison only, worth ×1.33 in the estimator's own favour; and the rate table's hour content relabelled without re-derivation, a relabelling its own author declined to certify. The unit of a comparison is part of the comparison, and it is an input on both sides.

Known direction of error

The curve is a normal approximation. Rate cells are right-skewed and correlated sums keep skew, so the true upper tail is fatter than drawn.

sections.title: Estimate gaps
sections.lead: Priced at zero, deliberately, each because a sensor refused rather than guessed. The estimate is understated by whatever these are worth, and that is the honest form.
sections.html:
elementitems unpricedwhy
System database schemas9The source names a platform and not one entity kind; the store's driver counts zero. Both repeats refused.
Non-delivery handling6The content is “what happens when there is no delivery” — a question, not an act. Both repeats refused.
Old-system integration interface7The source gives the word “integration” and names neither direction nor payload. Both repeats refused.
Core-parity scope baseline2Declares itself the boundary of “which core functions” and names none.
Seed items on the message store3The one named kind is created at run time; nothing is declared as pre-existing.
One element each, on opposite readings2 / 6The two repeats refused different elements — each had named the other's reading in its own doubts before choosing.

And a seventh, of a different kind

The rate author priced the parallel-run execution cycles against live traffic and explicitly excluded fixing the defects those cycles surface. Nothing else in the model prices that fixing: defect resolution is scoped to the ordinary test cycles, not to a shakeout against real message streams. Its own words: “if the estimator has no other home for those excluded things, the exclusions are holes, not savings.” There is no other home.

And one defect the estimate carries with its size named

The concept stage — discussions, immersion in the domain, technology selection — is priced at about 2% of the project. The outcome's owner later stated the actual parameter: all ten people, two months, nothing else, which is 17%. The row is low by ×8.5, and the cause is on the record and is not the rate author's fault: it correctly refused to price a stage from a calendar duration, then had to invent a headcount to convert calendar into effort. Stage headcount is a declaration parameter, not something a gap-blind rate author can be asked to assume. The centre above does not include the correction.

sections.title: Defaults
sections.lead: Where the source is silent, the technology declaration chooses — and each choice is written down as a fork with its own price, never inferred quietly.
sections.html:
acceptance
Direct to production, no acceptance stage
The definition of done names production traffic, tests agreeing with the old system, and the old version being decommissionable. It names no sign-off and no accepting party — this was an internal rework in a product company, with no client to accept. Declaring a UAT stage would invent one the source does not contain.
environments
Dev, stage, production
The source names no environment. Three are declared because two pinned obligations require the structure: integration tests run against the real message stream, which needs somewhere that is not production; and a promotion into production is demanded outright.
data
Seeded reference data, no legacy migration thinnest ground
A predecessor system exists, but no obligation names a data migration, and the storage infrastructure and database are declared reused. If the new system's stores in fact had to be loaded from the old one's, this declaration is wrong — and it is the largest of the four.
documentation
Operational and user documentation
The assumption log demands no documentation at all. It is declared anyway, from three pinned entries: a network operations centre that must be handed something to operate, a user-facing portal, and the requirement that the old version become decommissionable.

sections.title: Sensitivities carried, not resolved
sections.lead: Named in the assembly before the outcome was opened, so that nothing here could be invented afterwards.
sections.html:
structure
The second product model was never priced
The pair produced two models of the same obligations — 97 nodes and 87. Only the first was crossed, sized and priced. Unquantified width, named as such.
crossing
One crossing, no repeat
The three batches logged 20 judgement refusals against 50 filter refusals, plus 9 contested classifications. A second crossing could differ on those lines, and no repeatability reading exists for this step on this case.
R8
The total may be element count × a constant registered before the outcome
Two unrelated projects landed 7.7% apart at 17.3 and 15.0 person-days per element — a booking system from an RFP and a worldwide fax platform on a hand-built cluster. If the output is, to first order, element count times a constant, then it measures how finely the modeller chose to cut rather than the project. This was written down before the outcome was read, precisely so it could not be invented after.
one row
The highest calibration priority the rate author ever flagged
The adjudication of differences during the parallel run is priced per message type, because the true driver — distinct classes of difference — is unknowable in advance. The rate author flagged it with P/O = 10 and stated that its error is one-sided: it can understate and cannot overstate.
two rows
Adjudications on the desk, worth +333 person-days
The five unsizeable elements and thirteen closure violations (+182) and the four scope decisions (+151) are written down and unruled. Applied, they take the centre past the outcome rather than short of it.

sections.title: Where every number came from
sections.lead: Each sensor is an engine with a version, stamped on its own output. They are hired for what they are forbidden to see, not for autonomy — and on this case the thing they were forbidden to see was the outcome.
sections.html:
1
Product model ×2
52 pinned obligations → 97 elements. Two identical runs agreed on ×1.024 of anchored structure and placed all 47 product obligations wholly, with zero partial marks at closure.
2
Work model
Crossed against a declared technology → 570 items over 96 elements, plus four demanded-work branches. 70 refusals, each labelled filter or judgement.
3
Size classes ×2
74 of 79 sized in each repeat — but not the same five. Ten element-class divergences of 79, which after pricing is ×1.033 on the total.
4
Rate table uncalibrated
External norms, gap-blind. Eleven extra rows were needed for demanded work no dimension absorbs; the rate author refused all four as single rows on the first round, gave decompositions, and on the second wrote nine rows refusing none. It also caught a duration hiding inside one of them and quarantined it.
5
The outcome sealed
Held in a sealed file that no sensor and no prompt ever contained, opened only after the assembly document was written and closed. That document states so in its own first paragraph, and that sentence is the check.

What did not run on this case

Steps B, C and D never ran here, so the centre is table-priced and uncalibrated — on the other case the same chain gained ×1.415 from that step. And the reference class has not run in this generation, so there is no second opinion. Both are gaps in the case, not in the method.

The declaration is now required, not volunteered

Every role that produces a number moved to .1 on 2026-08-26. The change is the same in each: before any figure it must state its unit, whether leave sits inside it, whose roles are counted, and how far its own sources disagree with each other — and it must not restate its values in a convention foreign to its evidence to match the rest of the pipeline. The diagnostician's .1 is the consumer side: reconcile the declarations and size the units component of a gap before attributing the rest to method.

Nothing about how any of them estimates changed. This closes the failure that has cost this project more than any other — two numbers in different units compared as though they were in one — by making the thing that prevents it a required output rather than something a run happens to mention.

fine: What this report is not. Not a validated price, and not a price at all — it is work content in person-days. The centre is uncalibrated: Steps B–D never ran on this case, and the rate table behind it is external industry norms calibrated against no outcome. There is no second opinion here; the reference class has not run on this case in this generation.

What it is. The one comparison this project has against something that actually happened. The estimate was closed before the outcome was opened, nothing was fitted on it, and the miss is ×1.17 — carrying a known ×8.5 under-pricing of one stage and seven named holes priced at zero.
